title: A Breaking Point for the U.S. Auto Industry

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重塑者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店当DJ的黑胶唱片时代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每晚都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重塑者》吧。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Later this week, as many as 150,000 U.S.
sentences.zh: 本周晚些时候，多达15万名美国

sentences.en: auto workers may begin a historic strike against their employers, carmakers collectively known as the big three.
sentences.zh: 汽车工人可能会对他们的雇主——也就是统称为“三巨头”的汽车制造商——发起一场历史性的罢工。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague, Neil Beaudet, on the tangled decades-long dynamic that explains why such a walkout looks increasingly likely.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事尼尔·博代特将带我们了解这几十年来纠缠不清的动态，解释为什么这种罢工看起来越来越不可避免。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, September 12th.
sentences.zh: 今天是9月12日，星期二。

sentences.en: Neil, we are here to talk with you about a very big potential strike.
sentences.zh: 尼尔，我们今天请你来聊聊一场潜在的大规模罢工。

sentences.en: And it occurs to me that this has already been a summer of uniquely intense labor activism in the United States.
sentences.zh: 我意识到，今年夏天美国劳工运动的活跃程度异常高涨。

sentences.en: It has.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It's been quite a summer.
sentences.zh: 这是一个相当不平凡的夏天。

sentences.en: The Hollywood writers went out on strike.
sentences.zh: 好莱坞编剧们发起了罢工。

sentences.en: They were followed by the Hollywood actors.
sentences.zh: 紧接着是好莱坞演员们。

sentences.en: They're still on strike.
sentences.zh: 他们现在还在罢工。

sentences.en: The Teamsters and UPS were negotiating a contract.
sentences.zh: 卡车司机工会和UPS当时正在进行合同谈判。

sentences.en: There was a threat of a strike there.
sentences.zh: 那里也曾面临罢工威胁。

sentences.en: In the end, they did come up with a contract.
sentences.zh: 最终，他们达成了一份合同。

sentences.en: There was a local hotel strike in Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 洛杉矶还发生了一场当地酒店业的罢工。

sentences.en: So it's been a really busy summer in terms of labor movement.
sentences.zh: 所以，就劳工运动而言，这是一个非常忙碌的夏天。

sentences.en: And now we're coming to what could be the biggest labor conflict of the year.
sentences.zh: 现在我们正面临今年可能最大的一场劳资冲突。

sentences.en: And that's a potential strike between Ford, GM, and Stellantis, which is the parent of Chrysler, on one side, and the United Auto Workers on the other side.
sentences.zh: 那就是福特、通用汽车和克莱斯勒的母公司斯泰兰蒂斯，与全美汽车工人联合会（UAW）之间可能发生的罢工。

sentences.en: And why might this be the biggest?
sentences.zh: 为什么这可能是最大的一场？

sentences.en: Because the auto industry is a big piece of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 因为汽车工业是美国经济的

sentences.en: economy.
sentences.zh: 重要组成部分。

sentences.en: It's the largest manufacturing sector.
sentences.zh: 它是最大的制造业部门。

sentences.en: It employs 150,000 UAW workers.
sentences.zh: 它雇佣了15万名UAW工人。

sentences.en: And the union is threatening to strike all three companies at the same time.
sentences.zh: 而且工会威胁要同时对这三家公司发起罢工。

sentences.en: It's never done that before.
sentences.zh: 这在以前从未有过。

sentences.en: And the impact would be significant.
sentences.zh: 其影响将是巨大的。

sentences.en: It would cost the automakers billions of dollars in lost revenue and profit.
sentences.zh: 这将导致汽车制造商损失数十亿美元的收入和利润。

sentences.en: There would be a ripple effect among their hundreds of suppliers.
sentences.zh: 这会给数以百计的供应商带来连锁反应。

sentences.en: And in the Midwestern states, it could bring local economies to a halt.
sentences.zh: 在中西部各州，这可能会导致当地经济陷入停滞。

sentences.en: And is a strike likely, Neil?
sentences.zh: 尼尔，罢工发生的可能性大吗？

sentences.en: I think a strike is almost certain.
sentences.zh: 我认为罢工几乎是肯定的。

sentences.en: You have these two sides, the United Auto Workers and the three companies, that have a long and fraught history with each other.
sentences.zh: 全美汽车工人联合会和这三家公司之间有着一段漫长且充满摩擦的历史。

sentences.en: It's kind of like a marriage that has had its ups and downs and its trauma and pain.
sentences.zh: 这就像一段经历过起起落落、创伤和痛苦的婚姻。

sentences.en: And it is all coming to a head in these contract talks that are coming down to the wire.
sentences.zh: 而现在，在这些迫在眉睫的合同谈判中，一切都到了紧要关头。

sentences.en: Well, Neil, tell us about the history, the trauma and the pain of this long, complicated marriage between the big three automakers and the UAW,
sentences.zh: 那么，尼尔，给我们讲讲“三巨头”汽车制造商与UAW之间这段漫长而复杂的婚姻历史、创伤和痛苦吧，

sentences.en: this union that represents their workers, and why, in your mind, it might result in a strike that could shake the economy.
sentences.zh: 这个代表他们工人的工会，以及为什么在你看来，这可能会导致一场撼动经济的罢工。

sentences.en: What's that backstory?
sentences.zh: 背景故事是什么？

sentences.en: So, if we go back to the 1960s, the big three automakers were practically the entire U.S.
sentences.zh: 如果我们回到20世纪60年代，“三巨头”汽车制造商几乎就是整个美国

sentences.en: auto industry.
sentences.zh: 汽车工业的全部。

sentences.en: They made nine out of every ten cars that were sold in the United States.
sentences.zh: 在美国销售的每十辆车中，有九辆是他们制造的。

sentences.en: And because of that, the union had a great deal of power.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，工会拥有巨大的权力。

sentences.en: If they went out on strike, they could shut down a whole chunk of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 如果他们罢工，他们就能让美国汽车工业的

sentences.en: auto industry.
sentences.zh: 很大一部分陷入瘫痪。

sentences.en: And, in fact, that happened in 1970.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这种情况在1970年就发生过。

sentences.en: The negotiations go on in Detroit with little hope of averting a strike and more than half a dozen General Motors plants in the United States and Canada.
sentences.zh: 底特律的谈判在几乎无法避免罢工的希望中进行，美国和加拿大的六家通用汽车工厂受到影响。

sentences.en: We feel that we work hard in the shop, building these good cars for General Motors and for the customers.
sentences.zh: 我们觉得我们在车间里努力工作，为通用汽车和客户制造这些好车。

sentences.en: And we feel that if this is the way that we have to do, we have to strike, then we're going to hit the street.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不得不这样做，不得不罢工，那我们就会走上街头。

sentences.en: They were on strike against GM for 67 days.
sentences.zh: 他们对通用汽车进行了为期67天的罢工。

sentences.en: General Motors has been on strike for more than two weeks now.
sentences.zh: 通用汽车的罢工已经持续了两周多了。

sentences.en: And in Flint, Michigan, a GM strike takes $8 million a week out of the economy.
sentences.zh: 在密歇根州弗林特市，通用汽车的罢工每周从经济中抽走800万美元。

sentences.en: And it really shook the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这确实撼动了美国

sentences.en: economy and brought most of the auto industry to a halt.
sentences.zh: 经济，并使大部分汽车工业陷入停滞。

sentences.en: Good evening.
sentences.zh: 晚上好。

sentences.en: General Motors and the United Auto Workers have announced tentative agreement on a new three-year contract,
sentences.zh: 通用汽车和全美汽车工人联合会宣布就一份新的三年期合同达成初步协议，

sentences.en: an agreement that would end the strike, which has now threatened the nation's economy.
sentences.zh: 这份协议将结束这场已经威胁到国家经济的罢工。

sentences.en: And that win in 1970 was just one of a series of victories for the union in contract negotiations.
sentences.zh: 1970年的那次胜利只是工会在合同谈判中一系列胜利中的一次。

sentences.en: The new contract calls for a three-year increase in wages and fringe benefits, which would give the auto workers an extra $1.80 an hour
sentences.zh: 新合同要求在三年内增加工资和附加福利，这将使汽车工人每小时多赚1.80美元，

sentences.en: and would cost GM in the third year an extra billion and a half dollars.
sentences.zh: 并且在第三年将使通用汽车额外花费15亿美元。

sentences.en: They got increased wages and increasingly richer benefits.
sentences.zh: 他们获得了更高的工资和越来越丰厚的福利。

sentences.en: Their health care is almost totally covered by the companies.
sentences.zh: 他们的医疗保健几乎完全由公司承担。

sentences.en: So what happened was the auto workers were able to live a very comfortable middle-class life.
sentences.zh: 所以发生的情况是，汽车工人能够过上非常舒适的中产阶级生活。

sentences.en: They could send their kids to college, have a cottage on the lake and a boat.
sentences.zh: 他们可以送孩子上大学，在湖边有小屋，还有船。

sentences.en: And it really set the standard for middle-class people in the United States and helped lift the wages of non-union workers and other unionized workers in different industries.
sentences.zh: 这确实为美国的中产阶级树立了标准，并帮助提高了其他行业非工会工人和工会工人的工资。

sentences.en: It feels like, in a sense, everybody was winning at this stage of the marriage, right?
sentences.zh: 感觉在某种意义上，在这段婚姻的这个阶段，每个人都是赢家，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, the big three are selling almost every car being bought in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，“三巨头”卖掉了美国购买的几乎每一辆车。

sentences.en: They're doing well.
sentences.zh: 他们做得很好。

sentences.en: And because of the leverage that it has, the union and its workers are doing very well themselves.
sentences.zh: 而且由于其拥有的杠杆作用，工会及其工人自己也做得非常好。

sentences.en: Everybody's kind of winning.
sentences.zh: 每个人都算是赢家。

sentences.en: Yes, but then that starts to change.
sentences.zh: 是的，但随后情况开始改变。

sentences.en: These people all have one thing in common besides a happy smile.
sentences.zh: 这些人除了开心的笑容外，都有一个共同点。

sentences.en: They all own dependable Toyota Corollas.
sentences.zh: 他们都拥有可靠的丰田卡罗拉。

sentences.en: What happens is foreign competition arrives.
sentences.zh: 发生的事情是外国竞争对手来了。

sentences.en: All across the country, you'll see signs announcing the best gas mileage car in America, the Honda Civic 1300.
sentences.zh: 在全国各地，你会看到标语宣布美国最省油的汽车——本田思域1300。

sentences.en: Toyota and Honda start selling more and more cars in the United States and taking market share away from the big three.
sentences.zh: 丰田和本田开始在美国销售越来越多的汽车，并从“三巨头”手中夺取市场份额。

sentences.en: Toyota and then in the 80s, both Honda and Toyota and then others start building their own plants in the United States and they go to states where they can have non-union workers
sentences.zh: 丰田，然后在80年代，本田和丰田以及其他公司开始在美国建立自己的工厂，他们去那些可以雇佣非工会工人的州，

sentences.en: and pay lower wages.
sentences.zh: 并支付更低的工资。

sentences.en: And so suddenly the big three go from the 60s where they dominated the industry and were making a lot of money to a very difficult competitive situation
sentences.zh: 所以突然间，“三巨头”从60年代主导行业并赚取大量利润，转变为一个非常困难的竞争局面，

sentences.en: where they're losing market share.
sentences.zh: 他们正在失去市场份额。

sentences.en: They're woefully uncompetitive in terms of cost and especially on quality.
sentences.zh: 他们在成本方面，尤其是质量方面，表现得极其缺乏竞争力。

sentences.en: And so the balance in the industry starts to shift and Ford, GM and Chrysler are kind of reeling from the 80s on.
sentences.zh: 因此，行业内的平衡开始发生转变，福特、通用和克莱斯勒从80年代开始就有点摇摇欲坠了。

sentences.en: And this, I should acknowledge, is the era where I grew up in, the early and mid and late 80s.
sentences.zh: 我应该承认，这是我成长的时代，80年代初、中期和后期。

sentences.en: And I remember my mom showing up at home with a light blue Toyota Camry.
sentences.zh: 我记得我妈妈开着一辆浅蓝色的丰田凯美瑞出现在家里。

sentences.en: We had always previously owned American cars.
sentences.zh: 我们之前一直拥有美国车。

sentences.en: She bought into this vision, our whole family did, of the very reliable, dependable foreign car.
sentences.zh: 她接受了这种愿景，我们全家都接受了，即非常可靠、值得信赖的外国车。

sentences.en: And from then on out, we never owned American cars.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，我们再也没有买过美国车。

sentences.en: That is a really common experience for lots of people.
sentences.zh: 这对很多人来说是一个非常普遍的经历。

sentences.en: It happened in my family.
sentences.zh: 这发生在我家里。

sentences.en: My father bought a 1980 Chevy Citation, which was probably one of the worst cars ever made.
sentences.zh: 我父亲买了一辆1980年的雪佛兰Citation，这可能是有史以来最糟糕的汽车之一。

sentences.en: And it broke down so often that then he switched to Toyota.
sentences.zh: 它坏得太频繁了，所以他后来换成了丰田。

sentences.en: And then when I went to buy my first car, I bought a Honda.
sentences.zh: 然后当我买第一辆车时，我买了一辆本田。

sentences.en: And that happened for people all across the country.
sentences.zh: 全国各地的人们都发生了这种情况。

sentences.en: And what that did was alienated customers from the big three for almost a whole generation.
sentences.zh: 这导致消费者与“三巨头”疏远了几乎整整一代人。

sentences.en: So the big three are losing market share, but their workers are still doing relatively well.
sentences.zh: 所以“三巨头”正在失去市场份额，但他们的工人仍然做得相对较好。

sentences.en: And I'm going to assume that this is when the marriage starts to fray.
sentences.zh: 我假设这就是婚姻开始破裂的时候。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The workers are getting a relatively high pay and good benefits, but the big three are losing market share and they need to downsize.
sentences.zh: 工人们拿着相对较高的工资和良好的福利，但“三巨头”正在失去市场份额，他们需要裁员。

sentences.en: So the union is concerned about, well, when plants close, what happens to those workers?
sentences.zh: 所以工会担心，工厂关闭时，那些工人会怎样？

sentences.en: And they negotiate a deal in 1984 to create something they called the Jobs Bank.
sentences.zh: 于是他们在1984年谈判达成了一项协议，创建了一个他们称之为“就业银行”的东西。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 呵。

sentences.en: They would close a plant, but the workers would stay on the payroll, making most of their wages.
sentences.zh: 他们会关闭一家工厂，但工人会留在工资单上，领取大部分工资。

sentences.en: That does not sound very efficient.
sentences.zh: 这听起来效率不高。

sentences.en: It's not.
sentences.zh: 确实不高。

sentences.en: They had to report for work and more or less sit in a room and they could read books and play board games and hang out.
sentences.zh: 他们必须去上班，基本上坐在房间里，可以看书、玩棋盘游戏和闲逛。

sentences.en: And the automakers thought it would just be a temporary thing.
sentences.zh: 汽车制造商认为这只是暂时的。

sentences.en: They would only do this for a few years.
sentences.zh: 他们只会这样做几年。

sentences.en: They'd restructure.
sentences.zh: 他们会重组。

sentences.en: They'd come back better than ever.
sentences.zh: 他们会变得比以往任何时候都好。

sentences.en: They'd regain market share.
sentences.zh: 他们会重新获得市场份额。

sentences.en: And they would reopen these plants and they would need these workers.
sentences.zh: 他们会重新开放这些工厂，他们会需要这些工人。

sentences.en: But in the end, that didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 但最终，这并没有发生。

sentences.en: They never really regained their competitive edge.
sentences.zh: 他们从未真正恢复竞争优势。

sentences.en: And there were thousands of these workers on the payroll who were not producing cars.
sentences.zh: 而且工资单上有成千上万的工人没有生产汽车。

sentences.en: And so that put another big cost on their books.
sentences.zh: 这给他们的账目带来了另一个巨大的成本。

sentences.en: And so how do the big three deal with this?
sentences.zh: 那么“三巨头”是如何处理这个问题的呢？

sentences.en: That seems extremely expensive.
sentences.zh: 这看起来极其昂贵。

sentences.en: It is expensive.
sentences.zh: 确实很昂贵。

sentences.en: So they had to find ways to save money elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 所以他们必须想办法在其他地方省钱。

sentences.en: And they had to use cheaper materials and design cars that were less costly to produce.
sentences.zh: 他们不得不使用更便宜的材料，设计生产成本更低的汽车。

sentences.en: And so what you ended up with was some really crappy cars.
sentences.zh: 结果就是你得到了一些非常糟糕的汽车。

sentences.en: And I think if you talk to GM executives today, they will admit back in the day, they made some really crappy cars, but that was all they could do on the budget they had.
sentences.zh: 我想如果你今天和通用汽车的高管交谈，他们会承认过去他们制造了一些非常糟糕的汽车，但那是他们在预算范围内唯一能做到的。

sentences.en: And so it just made the competitive problem get even worse.
sentences.zh: 所以这只会让竞争问题变得更糟。

sentences.en: Right, because if you're already struggling to keep up with a more dependable foreign import like Toyota and your solution is to make crappy cars with cheaper materials,
sentences.zh: 没错，因为如果你已经在努力追赶像丰田这样更可靠的外国进口车，而你的解决方案是用更便宜的材料制造糟糕的汽车，

sentences.en: you're not going to close that gap.
sentences.zh: 你是不可能缩小差距的。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Okay, so what happens next?
sentences.zh: 好吧，接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, they get to the mid-2000s and they're really struggling to make money.
sentences.zh: 嗯，到了2000年代中期，他们真的很难赚钱。

sentences.en: In one year, Ford loses $12 billion.
sentences.zh: 有一年，福特亏损了120亿美元。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And they come to the contract talks in 2007 and the automakers go to the union.
sentences.zh: 他们在2007年的合同谈判中来到谈判桌前，汽车制造商找到了工会。

sentences.en: They explain that they are in dire straits, in danger of collapse.
sentences.zh: 他们解释说他们处于困境中，面临崩溃的危险。

sentences.en: They open their books and the union sees how bad it is and realize that they can't keep asking for more.
sentences.zh: 他们公开了账目，工会看到了情况有多糟糕，意识到他们不能再要求更多了。

sentences.en: They have to do something to help these companies get back on their feet.
sentences.zh: 他们必须做点什么来帮助这些公司重新站稳脚跟。

sentences.en: We're learning more about the concessions
sentences.zh: 我们正在了解更多关于让步的信息，

sentences.en: UAW workers will be asked to make at the Ford Claycomo plant.
sentences.zh: UAW工人将被要求在福特Claycomo工厂做出让步。

sentences.en: And that's when you have two measures that really make a big impact.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，你有两项措施产生了巨大的影响。

sentences.en: One is the union agrees to let the automakers hire new workers at about $15 an hour.

sentences.en: That's about half of what the top union wage was, which was $28 an hour at that time.

sentences.en: And they also create a trust fund to cover the cost of retiree health care.
sentences.zh: 他们还设立了一个信托基金来支付退休人员的医疗保健费用。

sentences.en: So this gets Ford, GM, and Chrysler out of the health care business.
sentences.zh: 所以这让福特、通用和克莱斯勒摆脱了医疗保健业务。

sentences.en: And that's a big burden off their books.
sentences.zh: 这对他们的账目来说是一个巨大的负担。

sentences.en: Now, UAW leadership told our Michael Mahoney today that they are not happy at all with this concession package.
sentences.zh: 现在，UAW领导层今天告诉我们的迈克尔·马奥尼，他们对这个让步方案一点也不满意。

sentences.en: Nonetheless, they are urging their rank and file to pass the package for fear that if they do not, that they could force Ford into bankruptcy.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，他们还是敦促普通成员通过该方案，因为担心如果不这样做，可能会迫使福特破产。

sentences.en: At that time, they also agreed to finally get rid of the jobs bank.
sentences.zh: 当时，他们还同意最终废除就业银行。

sentences.en: They came up with some terms where people who were in the jobs bank would take early retirement, and then they stopped putting people into the jobs bank.
sentences.zh: 他们达成了一些条款，让在就业银行的人提前退休，然后他们停止向就业银行输送人员。

sentences.en: Members of the United Auto Workers Union have ratified a package of concessions designed to reduce General Motors' labor costs.
sentences.zh: 全美汽车工人联合会（UAW）的成员已经批准了一揽子旨在降低通用汽车劳动力成本的让步方案。

sentences.en: It's a huge inflection point for the industry because for decades, it had always been more, more, more for the union.
sentences.zh: 这对该行业来说是一个巨大的转折点，因为几十年来，工会一直都在争取更多、更多、更多的利益。

sentences.en: And this is a point where finally that stops and the union has to take a step back from the kind of wages and benefit gains that they've been used to.
sentences.zh: 而现在，这一切终于停止了，工会不得不从他们习以为常的工资和福利增长中退后一步。

sentences.en: What once seemed impossible is now all but inevitable.
sentences.zh: 曾经看似不可能的事情，现在几乎已成定局。

sentences.en: General Motors is expected to officially file for bankruptcy tomorrow morning.
sentences.zh: 通用汽车预计将于明天上午正式申请破产。

sentences.en: The next thing that happened was the financial crisis.
sentences.zh: 接下来发生的事情就是金融危机。

sentences.en: Chrysler will receive billions in bailout money from the federal government.
sentences.zh: 克莱斯勒将从联邦政府获得数十亿美元的救助资金。

sentences.en: The company will enter bankruptcy to clear its books of debt that it couldn't bargain away.
sentences.zh: 该公司将进入破产程序，以清理那些无法通过谈判解决的债务。

sentences.en: They get some more changes to their labor terms and go through a deep restructuring.
sentences.zh: 他们对劳动条款进行了更多调整，并经历了深度的重组。

sentences.en: And finally, these companies are freed of the things that have been weighing them down for so long, and they're freed to go back to focusing on making good cars
sentences.zh: 最终，这些公司摆脱了长期以来拖累他们的包袱，得以重新专注于制造优质汽车，

sentences.en: and competing against their foreign rivals.
sentences.zh: 并与外国竞争对手展开竞争。

sentences.en: And does that actually happen?
sentences.zh: 但这真的发生了吗？

sentences.en: Do they become more competitive?
sentences.zh: 他们变得更有竞争力了吗？

sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They're able to put a lot more money into design and nicer materials, so they have these plush interiors.
sentences.zh: 他们能够投入更多的资金用于设计和更好的材料，所以他们拥有了这些豪华的内饰。

sentences.en: They develop fuel-efficient engines and new transmissions.
sentences.zh: 他们开发了省油的发动机和新的变速箱。

sentences.zh: 而且他们不再制造劣质汽车，开始制造非常好的汽车。

sentences.en: First rule of taking the world by surprise?
sentences.zh: 让世界感到惊讶的第一法则是什么？

sentences.en: Do something the world will actually notice.
sentences.zh: 做一些世界真正会注意到的事情。

sentences.zh: 隆重推出全新的福特 Fusion。

sentences.zh: 福特 Fusion 经过重新设计后推出，确实非常引人注目。

sentences.en: It's an entirely new idea of what a car can be.
sentences.zh: 它对汽车可以是什么样提出了一个全新的概念。

sentences.en: GM did the same thing with the Chevy Malibu.
sentences.zh: 通用汽车在雪佛兰迈锐宝上也做了同样的事情。

sentences.en: Here's a fact.
sentences.zh: 这是一个事实。

sentences.en: Chevrolet Malibu has better highway fuel efficiency than Honda Accord or Toyota Camry.

sentences.en: And then the market starts to shift to trucks and SUVs, which is really their forte.
sentences.zh: 随后市场开始转向卡车和 SUV，这确实是他们的强项。

sentences.en: And...
sentences.zh: 而且……

sentences.zh: 到 2015 年至 2016 年，他们创造了创纪录的利润。

sentences.zh: 这是一个处于当前市场最佳位置的公司的完美例子。

sentences.en: In the last five years or so,
sentences.zh: 在过去五年左右的时间里，

sentences.zh: 通用汽车每年的利润接近或超过 100 亿美元，这在几年前是无法想象的。

sentences.en: We're finally seeing scale and profitability at General Motors.
sentences.zh: 我们终于看到了通用汽车的规模和盈利能力。

sentences.en: The first time we've seen such things in all of their regions in many, many years.
sentences.zh: 这是我们多年来第一次在他们所有地区看到这样的情况。

sentences.en: So it becomes like this golden era for the big three automakers.
sentences.zh: 所以这成为了三大汽车制造商的黄金时代。

sentences.en: So the lesson here seems to be very clear that once unshackled from uncompetitive labor costs and labor contracts that provide for things like a jobs bank
sentences.zh: 因此，这里的教训似乎非常明确：一旦摆脱了缺乏竞争力的劳动力成本和提供诸如就业银行之类条款的劳动合同，

sentences.en: that are deeply inefficient, the big three can plow money into their actual products, the cars they make, and they make them beautifully and high-performing,
sentences.zh: 那些效率极低的条款，三大车企就可以将资金投入到他们实际的产品中，即他们制造的汽车，而且他们制造的汽车既美观又高性能，

sentences.en: and it sounds like reliable, and people want to buy them, and the companies thrive.
sentences.zh: 听起来也很可靠，人们想买它们，公司也就蓬勃发展了。

sentences.en: True.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Except for the workers, they look at these profits and think, hey, wait a minute, when are we going to get back what we gave to the companies, the concessions that we made?
sentences.zh: 除了工人们，他们看着这些利润心想，嘿，等一下，我们什么时候才能拿回我们让给公司的东西，那些我们做出的让步？

sentences.en: When are we going to see our wages rising as fast as the profits are rising?
sentences.zh: 我们什么时候才能看到我们的工资像利润一样快速增长？

sentences.en: And suddenly, they get a new union leader, and he tells them, you're right, we are going to fight.
sentences.zh: 突然间，他们有了一位新的工会领导人，他告诉他们，你们是对的，我们要抗争。

sentences.en: We are going to get back what we've given up.
sentences.zh: 我们要拿回我们放弃的东西。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.zh: 我在凌晨 4 点 30 分给总统打了电话，他接听了。

sentences.zh: 太空中的七十年。

sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: Sunil, tell us about this new labor boss.
sentences.zh: 苏尼尔，跟我们讲讲这位新的工会老板。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: His name is Sean Fain, and he comes to power in a really interesting way.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫肖恩·费恩，他上台的方式非常有趣。

sentences.en: Before, the union president was elected by a group of delegates who were more or less chosen by the union president and his associates.
sentences.zh: 以前，工会主席是由一群代表选出的，这些代表或多或少是由工会主席及其同僚挑选的。

sentences.en: And it was a patronage system.
sentences.zh: 那是一个恩庇制度。

sentences.en: You know, you do a favor for the boss, you get a good job in the union hierarchy.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你帮老板一个忙，就能在工会等级制度中得到一份好工作。

sentences.en: And it was not a democracy.
sentences.zh: 那根本不是民主。

sentences.en: And so, these leaders, over time, were not really responsive to what the members wanted.
sentences.zh: 所以，随着时间的推移，这些领导人并没有真正回应成员们的需求。

sentences.en: And you had a series of contracts,
sentences.zh: 你经历了一系列合同，

sentences.en: 2019, that didn't address what the rank and file were calling for.
sentences.zh: 2019 年，都没有解决普通工人们呼吁的问题。

sentences.en: And at the same time,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，

sentences.en: there was a lot of corruption in the union.
sentences.zh: 工会内部存在大量腐败。

sentences.en: Well, from a lakefront house built up north just for him to months-long stays at a Palm Springs resort.
sentences.zh: 嗯，从专门为他建造的北部湖畔别墅，到在棕榈泉度假村长达数月的逗留。

sentences.en: And the feds say
sentences.zh: 联邦调查局说，

sentences.en: Dennis Williams didn't pay a dime for it.
sentences.zh: 丹尼斯·威廉姆斯一分钱都没付。

sentences.en: There were two past presidents and other senior officials who used union money for golf vacations.
sentences.zh: 有两位前任主席和其他高级官员利用工会资金去打高尔夫度假。

sentences.en: Former UAW president
sentences.zh: 前 UAW 主席

sentences.en: Gary Jones has been charged in the corruption scandal that's rocked the union.
sentences.zh: 加里·琼斯因震撼工会的腐败丑闻而被起诉。

sentences.en: They bought high-priced liquors, all kinds of expensive apparel, expensive cigars.
sentences.zh: 他们购买高价烈酒、各种昂贵的服装、昂贵的雪茄。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And it has caused all kinds of ripples, lots of firings, and now the possibility of some major jail time.
sentences.zh: 这引起了各种连锁反应，很多人被解雇，现在还有可能面临严重的牢狱之灾。

sentences.en: And these two presidents were actually sent to jail.
sentences.zh: 这两位主席确实被送进了监狱。

sentences.en: And because of this corruption, there's a federal investigation, and the upshot of that is, finally...
sentences.zh: 由于这种腐败，联邦进行了调查，结果就是，终于……

sentences.en: We are following breaking news from overnight as the United Auto Workers are just a few votes away from naming a new president.
sentences.zh: 我们正在关注隔夜的突发新闻，全美汽车工人联合会距离提名新主席仅差几票。

sentences.en: The union has their first direct election for a UAW president, and this outsider,
sentences.zh: 工会进行了首次 UAW 主席直接选举，而这位局外人，

sentences.en: Sean Fain, eventually wins in a runoff by a razor-thin margin.
sentences.zh: 肖恩·费恩，最终以微弱优势在决选中获胜。

sentences.en: Today we say, no corruption, no concessions, no tears.
sentences.zh: 今天我们要说，没有腐败，没有让步，没有眼泪。

sentences.en: Our job, starting here and now, is to unite the UAW and get back in the fight.
sentences.zh: 我们的工作，从此时此地开始，就是团结 UAW 并重返战斗。

sentences.en: This is about ending sell-out unionism and ending company control.
sentences.zh: 这是为了结束出卖工会的行径，结束公司的控制。

sentences.en: It is an honor of a lifetime to be elected to lead our union, and I'll never forget that the first time the members of the UAW were given the right to vote, we chose change,
sentences.zh: 当选领导我们的工会是我一生的荣幸，我永远不会忘记，当 UAW 成员第一次获得投票权时，我们选择了改变，

sentences.en: we chose to fight.
sentences.zh: 我们选择了抗争。

sentences.en: And so for the first time in the long
sentences.zh: 所以，在 UAW 漫长的

sentences.en: 80-plus-year history of the UAW, they have a democratically elected leader chosen by the members themselves.
sentences.zh: 80 多年历史上，他们第一次拥有了一位由成员亲自选出的民主选举产生的领导人。

sentences.en: So tell us about this first truly democratically elected leader of the UAW,
sentences.zh: 那么跟我们讲讲这位 UAW 首位真正民主选举产生的领导人，

sentences.en: Sean Fain.
sentences.zh: 肖恩·费恩。

sentences.en: Sean Fain is 54.
sentences.zh: 肖恩·费恩今年 54 岁。

sentences.en: He is an electrician.
sentences.zh: 他是一名电工。

sentences.en: He worked at Chrysler for many years, and then he himself got a position in the union administration.
sentences.zh: 他在克莱斯勒工作多年，后来他自己也在工会管理层获得了一个职位。

sentences.en: His grandfather was also a union worker, and he carries around his grandfather's very first pay stub from when he started working as a union laborer years and years ago,
sentences.zh: 他的祖父也是一名工会工人，他随身带着他祖父多年前刚开始做工会劳工时的第一张工资单，

sentences.en: and he carries that around because that's his identity.
sentences.zh: 他随身带着它，因为那是他的身份认同。

sentences.en: He really identifies himself as a working-class person with working-class values, and he keeps that pay stub to remind him of that.
sentences.zh: 他确实将自己视为一个拥有工人阶级价值观的工人阶级人士，他保留那张工资单是为了提醒自己这一点。

sentences.en: So from the moment that he started campaigning, he promised the members that he was going to fight.
sentences.zh: 所以从他开始竞选的那一刻起，他就向成员们承诺他会抗争。

sentences.en: If he were elected, the union would go back to their more confrontational, more aggressive ways, and he promised them he was going to get back what they have given up.
sentences.zh: 如果他当选，工会将回到他们更具对抗性、更激进的方式，他向他们承诺他会拿回他们放弃的东西。

sentences.en: So given that fighting spirit and that combativeness that he promises from the start, as this latest negotiation with the big three gets underway, over these past few months,
sentences.zh: 鉴于他从一开始就承诺的那种战斗精神和好斗性，随着最近与三大车企的谈判在过去几个月里展开，

sentences.en: what exactly is Fain demanding from the companies?
sentences.zh: 费恩到底在向公司要求什么？

sentences.en: He wants a significant increase in the hourly wage.
sentences.zh: 他要求大幅提高时薪。

sentences.en: He has made an opening bid of 40%.
sentences.zh: 他提出了 40% 的开价。

sentences.en: Big raise.
sentences.zh: 大幅加薪。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He points to the CEOs of the three companies, and on average, between them, their compensation has gone up 40% over the last four years.
sentences.zh: 他指着这三家公司的首席执行官说，平均而言，他们的薪酬在过去四年里增长了 40%。

sentences.en: So he says, if the CEOs get 40%, we deserve 40%.
sentences.zh: 所以他说，如果首席执行官能得到 40%，我们也应该得到 40%。

sentences.en: He's probably not going to get that and probably knows that, but that's what he's aiming for.
sentences.zh: 他可能不会得到那么多，也可能知道这一点，但这就是他的目标。

sentences.en: He also wants to restore retiree health care paid by the companies.
sentences.zh: 他还希望恢复由公司支付的退休人员医疗保健。

sentences.en: He wants to have a new kind of jobs bank if plants close.
sentences.zh: 他希望在工厂关闭时建立一种新的就业银行。

sentences.en: And he wants to undo this wage structure that was put in place where entry-level workers get paid significantly less than veteran workers.
sentences.zh: 他希望废除现行的工资结构，即入门级工人的工资远低于资深工人。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: What else?
sentences.zh: 还有什么？

sentences.en: And one of the most contentious things that he has raised is this idea of allowing workers to work four days a week but get paid for five.
sentences.zh: 他提出的最具争议的问题之一是允许工人每周工作四天但领取五天工资的想法。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And what he's really aiming at is that there are workers in some plants who are working six days a week, seven days a week, sometimes 10-hour days,
sentences.zh: 他真正针对的是，有些工厂的工人每周工作六天、七天，有时每天工作 10 小时，

sentences.en: 12-hour days.
sentences.zh: 12 小时。
